scope: All stories tagged ARC-STORM, ARC-WATER or ARC-HEALTH (112 stories, days -55 to 110), read in day order as the hurricane, water-crisis and public-health storylines; key timing facts (landfall, category, surge, bridge closure/reopening, outages, boil-water notice and instructions, parts delay/arrival, notice lifted, hardening plan) also grep-checked across all 393 stories.

findings.old: Bring tap water to a rolling boil for one minute before drinking it
findings.new: Bring tap water to a rolling boil for two minutes before drinking it
findings.reason: Boil instruction contradicts the notice (PUB-039: rolling boil for two minutes) and every other story, including this reporter's own Sept. 18 explainer (P004-02).
findings.resolution: Verified resolved by another reviewer's fix (checked 2026-11-08).

findings.old: Bring it to a rolling boil for one minute and let it cool.
findings.new: Bring it to a rolling boil for two minutes and let it cool.
findings.reason: Boil instruction contradicts PUB-039 (two minutes) and Harborline's own notice story (P004-01) and checklists (P008-03, P010-02, P032-01).
findings.resolution: Verified resolved by another reviewer's fix (checked 2026-11-08).

findings.old: Washing your hands with soap and tap water is OK for everyday hand-washing.
findings.new: For hand-washing, use soap and boiled or bottled water when you can.
findings.reason: Only story telling readers tap water is fine for hand-washing; every later story (P006-01, P008-01, Harborline's own P008-03, P010-04 "Shah's advice hasn't changed", P014-01, P020-02, P028-01, P029-01) says soap and boiled or bottled water.

findings.old: The utility said last month that the shipment was coming from out of state.
findings.new: The utility said earlier this month that the shipment was coming from out of state.
findings.reason: Date error: the delay was announced Mon., Oct. 4 (PUB-055, day 20; P020-02); this story runs Wed., Oct. 20, the same month.

findings.old: , weeks behind schedule
findings.new: after weeks of delay
findings.reason: No arrival date or schedule was ever made public (utility and supplier repeatedly declined to give one: P020-02, P021-02); "behind schedule" implies the non-public quoted lead time.

findings.old: The parts Corpus Christi has waited on for more than a month
findings.new: The parts Corpus Christi has waited on since September
findings.reason: The need for parts was first made public Sept. 24 (PUB-050), 26 days before arrival; the order date is not public, so "more than a month" overstates the public wait.

findings.old: In September, she organized her neighbors' runs to water distribution sites.
findings.new: This fall, she organized her neighbors' runs to water distribution sites.
findings.reason: Ramos ran her street's water runs for the whole notice, Sept. 18 to Oct. 23 (canon; P037-01, P039-01), not only in September.

findings.old: More than three weeks of boiling, hauling and cleaning take a toll on everyone.
findings.new: Three weeks of boiling, hauling and cleaning take a toll on everyone.
findings.reason: Notice issued Sept. 18; on Oct. 8 that is 20 days. Same-day Ledger story P024-02 says residents are "nearing three weeks of boiling water."

findings.old: Leticia Ramos keeps the list on a clipboard by her front door: house numbers, how many people live in each, who has a car, who has a baby, who can't lift a case of water.
findings.new: By Leticia Ramos' front door hangs a clipboard, and on it is her whole street: house numbers, household sizes, who drives, who has a newborn, who needs help lifting.
findings.reason: Lede nearly copies Coastline's Ramos lede two days earlier (P005-02: "...how many people live in each house, who has a baby, who can't lift a case of water"). New wording matches the "has car"/"needs help lifting" columns in P024-02.

findings.old: Hallway beds and hand sanitizer:
findings.new: What the hallway beds taught:
findings.reason: Health officials repeatedly said hand sanitizer does not work well against norovirus (P006-01, P008-01, P014-01, P028-01); the body never mentions sanitizer. Also the third Whitlock headline built on "Hallway beds and..." (P023-02).

findings.old: Alyssa Cortez can tell you exactly when she knew the boil-water weeks were going to be bad.
findings.new: Alyssa Cortez remembers the moment she knew the boil-water weeks were going to be bad.
findings.reason: Lede repeats the construction of the same reporter's Cortez profile 12 days earlier (P086-03: "Alyssa Cortez can tell you which week of the fall was the worst...").

findings.old: "Wash your hands, stay home when you're sick, and if you're still feeling bad after a few days, don't wait it out. Call your doctor," she said.
findings.new: "Soap, a sick day at home and an early call to your doctor if you're not getting better. That list hasn't changed," she said.
findings.reason: Shah quote nearly duplicates her quote in P086-03 ("Wash your hands, stay home when you're sick, and get your flu shot...").

findings.old: Stomach illness has eased, but health officials say keep boiling until the notice lifts
findings.new: With ER hallways clear again, health officials say keep boiling until the notice lifts
findings.reason: Near-duplicate of the same reporter's headline a week earlier (P028-01: "Stomach illness has eased, but the boil-water notice still matters").

findings.old: they remain about 40% above.
findings.new: they remain about 40% above normal.
findings.reason: Figure is clipped; PUB-069 and the body say "about 40% above normal."

findings.old: Countywide, emergency visits are back near normal. In low-income neighborhoods near the bay, they remain about 40% above.
findings.new: Countywide, emergency visits are back near normal, but low-income neighborhoods near the bay are running about 40% above normal.
findings.reason: Second sentence is identical to the same-day Ledger dek (P045-01) and drops "normal."

findings.old: flooding bays and setting off a tanker spill
findings.new: flooding bays as oil spills from moored tankers
findings.reason: Headline says the storm caused the spill; PUB-024 and this story's own body say the cause is under investigation. Coverage must stay neutral on cause.

findings.old: and setting off an oil spill at a terminal in the city's industrial Inner Harbor
findings.new: as oil spilled at a terminal in the city's industrial Inner Harbor
findings.reason: Lede says the storm set off the spill, contradicting "the cause was under investigation" two sentences later (PUB-024).

findings.old: The Harbor Bridge and Nueces Bay Causeway were closed after the storm, cutting Portland and North Beach off from downtown until inspections finished.
findings.new: The Harbor Bridge and Nueces Bay Causeway closed as Rafael's winds rose and stayed shut until inspections finished, cutting Portland and North Beach off from downtown.
findings.reason: The story is about a wind-closure review, which only makes sense if the bridges closed in the wind; "closed after the storm" conflicts with the companion story P110-02 ("The bridges closed as Rafael hit").

findings.old: It is fainter than it was the day after the storm, he says
findings.new: It is fainter than it was in the first days after the storm, he says
findings.reason: Bell canon and P042-02: the oil smell reached North Beach two days after landfall, not the day after.
